thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx across inference-gateway (us-west) - alert threshold 3% -> 12% in last 5m. Paging oncall (aria).
aria: got the page, on my way in. looking at grafana now. can someone post the alert link?
jamie: https://grafana.company.net/d/ai/ingest?orgId=1&panelId=24 - saw a spike in gateway 502/504s starting ~1729987400.
kevin: i'm seeing increased upstream resets from envoys, lots of retried requests piling up. CPU on lb nodes spiked too.
aria: timeline: alert at 1729987654, initial spike ~1729987400, sustained through now. impact: customer-facing inference latency and some timeouts. support flagged 5 customers hitting errors.
ops-mgr: @aria please confirm if this is routing or application error. any 5xx patterns? 502 vs 504 vs 503?
aria: logs show mostly 502 Bad Gateway and 5xx code from upstream with 'upstream reset' and 'too_many_retries' errors in envoy. stack traces point toward retry loop: client->edge LB->inference-gateway->backend pool A, B.
luis: quick snapshot from envoy stats:
```
cluster.inference-backendA.upstream_cx_total: 12000
cluster.inference-backendA.upstream_rq_retry: 9800
cluster.inference-backendA.upstream_cx_overflow: 0
cluster.inference-backendA.upstream_rq_5xx: 320
```
aria: that retry count is suspiciously high. did we recently change retry_policy in route rollout?
jamie: we did a canary of a new route config yesterday to force retries on 503s for some clients (opt-in). looks like the policy accidentally applied to the global route set.
kevin: yep, the canary selector was too broad: `header_match: X-Client-Type: alpha` matched empty headers for some requests -> retried everything. when upstream is overloaded, retries amplify load -> cascade 5xx.
aria: mitigation plan: 1) disable retries at edge immediately, 2) route traffic off the affected inference-gateway pool (drain) to fallback pool, 3) reduce route weight for problematic hosts. executing step 1 now.
aria: applying temp patch: `envoy config set /routes/global retry_policy: none` -> running.
aria: applied. monitoring.
incidents-bot: Config change detected by deploy-bot at 1729987705: routes/global retry_policy reverted to none (author: aria).
kevin: seeing retry counters drop within 30s. 5xx rate trending down from 12% -> 5% now.
luis: starting traffic shift: reducing weight for pool A from 0.7 -> 0.2 over 1 minute, shifting to fallback pool C. command: `trafficctl set-weight inference-poolA 0.2 --window 60s`
jamie: doing a quick health-check curl loop to verify:
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sS -D - https://inference.example.com/health | head -n 1; sleep 0.5; done
```
aria: OK health responses mostly 200 now, some intermittent 502s but much fewer. customer-reported errors dropping.
support-bot: Notifying CS: ticket #CS-4487 flagged high error rate, updating status -> mitigation in progress.
ops-mgr: good. please keep scaling knobs as last resort. we should avoid full rollback of canary unless necessary.
kevin: think we should also increase circuit breaker max_connections and max_requests on the gateway side to give graceful backpressure. lowered thresholds caused early ejects and then spin recovery loop.
aria: opening an incident in tracker: https://incidents.company.net/incident/INC-2024-198 - tagging SRE/infra/runtime. please add notes about the accidental canary selector.
aria: initial severity: Sev2 (customer impact, partial outage). will update after stabilization.
luis: metric update at 1729987780: 5xx -> 2.1%, p99 latency back to baseline.
jamie: rolling forward with a controlled canary rollback for the route-change PR: PR #5893 revert retry-policy change.
incidents-bot: Oncall handoff reminder: @kevin will stay as primary until next rotation at 1730000000.
kevin: i'll take primary, monitoring for 30m. follow-up tasks: 1) audit canary selectors for header-match fallthroughs, 2) add tighter unit test for route matcher, 3) run small chaos test for retry amplification.
ops-mgr: assign postmortem to jamie and aria, due EOD tomorrow. include customer impact timeline and list of affected customers.
aria: adding notes: affected customers: acme-inc, tensorflow-cloud, beta-testers 3. CS notified.
support-bot: CS updated: ticket CS-4487, 3 customers contacted with status page entry created: https://status.company.net/incidents/INF-2024-07
kevin: final check - all metrics stable for 5m, no new pager. I'll keep an eye and then call it mitigated.
aria: declaring mitigation at 1729987830, will keep monitoring for 60m then move to post-incident review. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2024-198 marked MITIGATED by kevin at 1729987830.
